flashcard_questions.a: Making a false statement about someone that damages their reputation.

flashcard_questions.q: Which form of defamation is written or published?
Which form of defamation is spoken in conversation?
Why do words in a broadcast count as libel rather than slander?
flashcard_questions.a: They are kept in a permanent form.
Creations of the mind that are protected by law.

flashcard_questions.q: Which intellectual property right protects original creative works?
Which intellectual property right protects logos, names and slogans?
Which intellectual property right protects inventions and technical processes?
When does copyright protection begin for a creative work?
flashcard_questions.a: The moment the work is created.
Licences that let a creator share work under set conditions such as attribution.
Limited use of copyrighted material for criticism, review, news reporting or education.

flashcard_questions.q: Whose agreement is needed before filming on private land?
When is consent needed to use a photograph of an identifiable person?
flashcard_questions.a: When the image is used commercially, for example in an advert.

flashcard_questions.q: How long may personal data be kept?
What can happen to a product that uses copyrighted material without permission?
flashcard_questions.a: It may have to be removed from distribution or destroyed.
